status_summary: Effective 2025-04-09, according to a Reuters report of an Acting Chairman memo, Enforcement staff began reporting to deputy directors for three regions plus specialized units instead of ten regional directors, and Examinations staff to new associate directors; the regional offices themselves were kept. The Chairman's 2025-06-03 Senate testimony confirms that Enforcement and Examinations reporting lines were realigned, says headcount fell 15 percent in the fiscal year, describes a flat request of $2.149 billion for about 4,100 FTE (447 fewer than FY2025), and says approval was being sought to disband the FinHub office. A final rule published 2026-07-20 (91 FR 45187) moved registration-related delegations from the Division of Examinations to the EDGAR Business Office. No agency-wide cut in direct reports to the Chairman or in managers per employee was found.

timeline.event: A reorganization took effect under which Enforcement staff report to deputy directors for three regions plus specialized units, replacing reporting to ten regional directors, and Examinations staff report to new associate directors (per Reuters).
In testimony the Chairman described the FY2026 request of $2.149 billion and about 4,100 FTE, realigned Enforcement and Examinations reporting lines, and a request for approval to disband FinHub.
The SEC published a final rule (91 FR 45187, effective 2026-07-26) moving registration-related delegated functions from the Division of Examinations to the EDGAR Business Office.

title: Streamline SEC management: core functions, fewer direct reports, merged offices
uncertainties: The Reuters article as hosted shows no date; the 2025 year is inferred from its reference to the Acting Chairman and the testimony's description of realigned reporting lines. No SEC press release on the reorganization was found in one search. The 2025-05-06 town hall remark that reorganization was to come is an announcement and is kept in sources only. Whether FinHub was disbanded was not confirmed. The FY2027 request and 2026 organization charts were not checked. Headcount cuts reflect buyouts and attrition as well as reorganization.
